title: Dissolution enthalpy of NaCl in water at 25 C, 45 C and 60 C. Determination of the Pitzer's parameters of the {H2O-NaCl} system and the molar dissolution enthalpy at infinite dilution of NaCl in water between 25 C and 100 C
authors: Nathalie Hubert, Roland Solimando, Alexandra Pere, Louis Schuffenecker
needs_pass2_reason: text layer was usable; every cell of Tables 1-4 matched the page images after the corrections listed (only decimal-comma/OCR-letter artefacts in the text layer, not in the numbers); page scan is clean
experimental_method: Batch differential calorimetry (SETARAM C80D, calibrated with the heat of fusion of indium) of the dissolution of dried solid NaCl in water at 24.4, 44.3 and 59.2 C up to saturation; water activity of NaCl(aq) at m=4.086 from a static vapour-pressure apparatus (earlier paper).
uncertainties_stated: precision of the calorimetric results about 2%; lowest salt molality 0.06 mol/kg set by calorimeter sensitivity; average relative error of fitted dissolution enthalpies about 2%; mean relative deviation of aw about 0.1%
quality_remarks: Heat sign: DeltaH_exp is printed positive (endothermic dissolution).
Table 1 (24.4 C) printed with 27 rows, Table 2 14, Table 3 13.
Conclusion text says {N2O-NaCl}, a misprint for {H2O-NaCl}.
Table 3 column header printed 'DeltaH_exp/n1 Delta_sol(m)' (the H dropped), meaning the same as in Tables 1-2.
Table 1 first row has the largest DeltaH_exp/n1 at low m; per-experiment scatter of order 2-5% visible (e.g. 4113 vs 4305).
Table 4 aw (exp.) values duplicate the authors' earlier paper (ref 10) and the column is used as validation; text says 133 values for 293.15-363.15 K and m 1-5.5, only m=4.086 is tabulated.
changes_after_image_check: text layer substituted decimal commas for points in the dH_exp columns of Table 1 (17,03 etc.), OCR letter o/t for 0/1 (o.1676, t735): all values written from the page image; no digit differed otherwise
extraction_notes: CSVs written from the page image reading (checked against text layer). Tables 1-3 are separate files, T constant from caption. In Table 4 only aw (exp.) is a datum. The mapping's 'm_final' key marks the molality as that of the final solution. Page image p-3 (journal 159) was theory only, no tables. Mapping property dh_sol with the value being the authors' division of the measured heat by n_1 (derived_by_authors) and the raw heat as value2, per the brief convention; a molar enthalpy is the reported result.
